headline: Composable Commerce & CMS Architect — React/Vue, AI-Accelerated Delivery

summary.p: Thinking about going composable, but not sure it's worth the cost and complexity? Already committed to a CMS but need someone to design content models your authors will actually enjoy? Or just need a senior React/Vue developer who moves fast without creating a mess?

15+ years as an architect and hands-on developer on e-commerce projects for brands like Vans, The North Face, PUMA, Zermatt Matterhorn Tourism and Citizen Watches, across e-comm platforms, headless CMS (Contentful, Amplience) and React/Vue front-ends talking to them via APIs.

Weighing composable vs your platform's built-in tools? I can help you evaluate whether it's worth it for your size and budget, not just implement whatever's trendy. That includes practical calls about where to store images (CMS, e-comm platform, or a dedicated DAM like Cloudinary), what actually belongs in a headless CMS vs your e-comm platform, and what a React/Next.js layer really costs to build and maintain.

If the architecture is set and you need schemas designed: powerful enough for what marketing needs, simple enough that authors don't need a manual. Feature-rich under the hood, intuitive on the surface - not a cockpit of 1,000 buttons.

I still write, review and ship code myself. I use Claude Code and sub-agents to move fast, review, test and enforce standards across codebases. I personally verify what actually ships to production: architecture decisions, performance impact and coding standards.

I've run my own ventures end-to-end, wearing every hat. I know what it's like with no one to hand a task to, so I ask the right questions, move with minimal direction, and take ownership. Comfortable owning the architecture conversation with stakeholders and being knee-deep in a POC the same afternoon.
